chitchat: Mrs Sloane resettles the ring of keys, which produces a noise the whole hall can hear.
She looks at the noticeboard for a while with an expression of settled disappointment.
She straightens a card in a letterbox slot that was already straight.
The timer light on the half-landing goes out. She does not turn it back on.
She listens to the ceiling for a moment, identifies which flat, and says nothing.
She moves two feet to the left, which somehow makes the stairs harder to get past.
"Thursday," she says, to nobody at all. "It has always been Thursday."
She wipes the top of the radiator with one finger and inspects the finger.
She tucks something behind the door that came for somebody who is out.
description: The caretaker, who is not paid to be and has never once said so. A small upright woman of about seventy with a very large ring of keys and an exact knowledge of who is behind on what. She stands in the hall rather than sits, because sitting down in the hall would imply she was waiting for something, and she is not waiting, she is simply there.

bins.text:
"I typed that." A long silence. "Four years ago."

She looks at the board as though it has personally disappointed her, which it has.

"Somebody's written on it. Somebody else has written on that. There is a third hand on there now that I do not recognise and I have lived in this building since it had a different name." The keys shift. "It goes out on the day. It has always gone out on the day. It is not complicated."

boiler.text:
"Doing its best," she says, with genuine feeling. "It heats four floors of basins and it was put in for two. There's a note on it in my hand saying not to bleed it yourself and every few years a young man in one of the flats decides he knows better, and then there is a great deal of noise and no hot water for a day and a half, and then he apologises to me in the hall."

A pause.

"I do accept the apology. I want to be clear I always accept it."

bye.text: A nod, and they go back to it before you have got the door open.

options.label: Is the park view any good?

root.text: "Six flats, four let, and the two that aren't are not going to you today, so don't start." She resettles the keys. "If you're visiting, the bell's the bell. If you're delivering, the ledge is the ledge."

text_by_relation.familiar:
She is at the foot of the stair with your name already half out of her mouth.

"There's a thing come for you and I've had it behind the door two days because I wasn't leaving it on the ledge in that rain." She produces it. "No, don't. I'd rather you didn't. Just take it up."
text_by_relation.first:
A small woman in a housecoat is standing in the middle of the hall doing nothing whatsoever, which she manages to make look like a job.

"Sloane. Mrs." The keys shift. "I'm not the landlord, before you ask, the landlord is a company and the company is a letter box in the Yards. I just have the keys and the boiler and everybody's post when they're out."

She looks you over, once, thoroughly.

"Park view. It's in the advertisement in larger letters than the rent, which tells you what they think of the rent."
text_by_relation.known: "Oh, it's you." The keys go still. "Number four's had their music on since eleven. I'm not saying anything. I'm telling you, which is different."

view.text:
"It is, and it's the reason the damp gets overlooked." She says it plainly, without any bitterness at all. "Front two on every floor look at the Green and the back two look at a wall about nine feet away. Same rent. Nobody who takes a back one stays more than a year, and nobody who takes a front one ever leaves, and the top front has had the same tenant since before my husband died."

She nods at the stair.

"That's why there's never anything to let. It's not popularity. It's that the good ones never come free."

clothing_layers: a housecoat with the pockets pulled out of shape by keys
a cardigan buttoned wrong at the bottom

name: Margit Sloane
